solutions.question: What are temporary and permanent magnets?
steps: A temporary magnet is a magnet that loses its magnetism soon after the magnetising force is removed.
A permanent magnet retains its magnetism for a long time after the magnetising force is removed.
solutions.answer: Temporary magnets lose their magnetism quickly, while permanent magnets retain it for a long time.

solutions.question: Define magnetic field of a magnet.
steps: The region around a magnet in which its magnetic force can be experienced is called the magnetic field of the magnet.
solutions.answer: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet in which its magnetic force can be experienced.

solutions.question: What are magnetic lines of force?
steps: Magnetic lines of force are imaginary lines used to represent a magnetic field.
The direction of a magnetic line of force is the direction in which a north pole would move.
Outside a magnet, these lines go from the north pole to the south pole.
solutions.answer: Magnetic lines of force are imaginary lines that represent the magnetic field and show its direction.

solutions.question: Name some uses of permanent magnets and electromagnets.
steps: Permanent magnets are used in compasses, loudspeakers and refrigerator doors.
Electromagnets are used in electric bells, relays and cranes for lifting scrap iron.
solutions.answer: Permanent magnets are used in compasses, loudspeakers and refrigerator doors; electromagnets are used in electric bells, relays and lifting cranes.

solutions.question: What are magnetic domains?
steps: A magnetic domain is a small region in a magnetic material in which the magnetic moments of atoms are aligned in the same direction.
An unmagnetised magnetic material has domains oriented in different directions.
solutions.answer: Magnetic domains are small regions in a magnetic material where the magnetic moments of atoms are aligned in the same direction.

solutions.question: Which type of magnetic field is formed by a current-carrying long coil?
steps: A current-carrying long coil (solenoid) produces a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet.
solutions.answer: A current-carrying long coil produces a bar-magnet-like magnetic field.

solutions.question: Differentiate between paramagnetic and diamagnetic materials.
steps: Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted by a magnet and become magnetised in the direction of the applied magnetic field.
Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by a magnet and become magnetised opposite to the direction of the applied magnetic field.
solutions.answer: Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted by a magnet; diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by it.

solutions.question: Two bar magnets are stored in a wooden box. Label the poles of the magnets and identify P and Q objects.
steps: Store the two bar magnets parallel to each other with unlike poles adjacent.
Label the poles so that one end has N above S and the other end has S above N.
Identify P and Q as soft-iron keepers placed across the ends of the magnets.
solutions.answer: P and Q are soft-iron keepers; the two magnets are stored with unlike poles adjacent.

solutions.question: A steel bar has to be magnetised by placing it inside a solenoid such that end A of a bar becomes N-pole and end B becomes S-pole. Draw circuit diagram of solenoid showing steel bar inside it.
steps: Place the steel bar AB inside a solenoid and connect the solenoid, a cell and a switch in series.
Choose the current direction so that, when viewed from end A, the current around the solenoid is anticlockwise.
By the end rule for a solenoid, an anticlockwise current at an end makes that end a north pole.
Therefore A becomes N and the opposite end B becomes S.
solutions.answer: The diagram shows a steel bar AB inside a solenoid connected in series with a cell and switch. Conventional current is anticlockwise when viewed from A, making A the north pole and B the south pole.

Electric current or motion of electrons produce magnetic field. Is the reverse process true, that is the magnetic field gives rise to electric current? If yes, give an example and describe it briefly.
steps: Yes. A changing magnetic field can produce an electric current in a conductor. This phenomenon is called electromagnetic induction.
For example, connect a coil to a galvanometer and move a bar magnet into or out of the coil.
The galvanometer shows a deflection while the magnet is moving, indicating that a current is induced in the coil.
The current is produced only while the magnetic field through the coil is changing.
solutions.answer: Yes; a changing magnetic field induces current, as when a magnet is moved into or out of a coil.

solutions.question: Four similar solenoids are placed in a circle as shown in the figure. The magnitude of current in all of them should be the same. Show by diagram, the direction of current in each solenoid such that when current in any one solenoid is switched OFF, the net magnetic field at the centre O is directed towards that solenoid. Explain your answer.
How can you identify whether an object is a magnet or a magnetic material?
steps: Bring one pole of a known magnet near the object.
Repulsion proves that the object is a magnet, because repulsion occurs only between like poles of two magnets.
Attraction alone does not prove that the object is a magnet, because a magnet also attracts magnetic materials such as iron, nickel and cobalt.
solutions.answer: Use the repulsion test: repulsion proves the object is a magnet; attraction alone does not.

solutions.question: Describe the strength of a magnetic field in terms of magnetic lines of force. Explain it by drawing a few diagrams for the fields as examples.
steps: Draw several magnetic field lines in each example, keeping the lines distinct and showing their relative spacing.
In a strong-field region, draw the lines close together; in a weak-field region, draw them farther apart.
For a uniform field, draw parallel lines with equal spacing.
Magnetic field strength is indicated by the density of field lines: the number of lines passing through unit area perpendicular to the field.
The closer the lines, the stronger the magnetic field; the farther apart they are, the weaker the field.
solutions.answer: A magnetic field is stronger where its lines of force are more densely spaced and weaker where they are more widely spaced. Parallel, equally spaced lines represent a uniform field.

solutions.question: What is a circuit breaker? Describe its working with the help of a diagram.
steps: A circuit breaker is an automatic safety switch that breaks a circuit when the current becomes excessive.
It is connected in series with the circuit it protects.
During an overload or short circuit, the large current produces a strong magnetic effect in the breaker’s electromagnet.
The electromagnet attracts an armature, separating the contacts and opening the circuit.
After the fault is removed, the breaker can be reset.
solutions.answer: A circuit breaker is an automatic switch that protects a circuit from excessive current. Excess current strengthens its electromagnet, which opens the contacts and breaks the circuit.

solutions.question: A magnet attracts only a magnet. Explain the statement.
steps: The statement is not correct if it means that a magnet attracts only another magnet.
A magnet also attracts magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt, even when they are not magnets.
Repulsion, however, occurs only between like poles of two magnets.
solutions.answer: A magnet attracts magnetic materials as well as magnets; repulsion is the sure test for identifying a magnet.

solutions.question: Differentiate between paramagnetic, diamagnetic and ferromagnetic materials with reference to the domain theory.
steps: Paramagnetic materials: The atoms behave like tiny magnets, but their magnetic moments are randomly oriented when no magnetic field is applied. In an external field, some moments align with the field, so the material is weakly attracted.

Diamagnetic materials: The atoms have no permanent magnetic moments. An external field induces magnetic moments opposite to the field, so the material is weakly repelled. They do not form permanent magnetic domains.

Ferromagnetic materials: Each material contains many small regions called domains. In each domain, the magnetic moments of atoms are aligned in the same direction. In an unmagnetized specimen, the domains are randomly oriented; an external field aligns more domains, producing strong magnetization.
solutions.answer: Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted, diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled, and ferromagnetic materials become strongly magnetized as their domains align.

solutions.question: Why ferromagnetic materials are suitable for making magnets?
steps: A ferromagnetic material consists of many small regions called domains, each containing atoms whose magnetic moments are aligned in the same direction.
In an unmagnetized specimen, the domains are randomly oriented, so their magnetic effects cancel.
When the material is placed in a magnetic field, the domains align with the field and the material becomes strongly magnetized.
Therefore, ferromagnetic materials are suitable for making magnets.
solutions.answer: Ferromagnetic materials are suitable for making magnets because their domains align to produce strong magnetization.

mcqs.stem: Which one of the following is not a magnetic material?
rationales: Cobalt is a magnetic material and is attracted to a magnet.
Iron is a magnetic material and is strongly attracted to a magnet.
Aluminium is not classed as a magnetic material in the usual school-level classification.
Nickel is a magnetic material and is attracted to a magnet.

Outside a magnet, field lines emerge from the north pole rather than enter it.

mcqs.stem: Permanent magnets cannot be made by:
rationales: Soft iron loses its magnetism readily, so it is unsuitable for making permanent magnets.
Steel retains magnetism and can be used to make permanent magnets.
Neodymium is used to make strong permanent magnets.
Alnico is an alloy used to make permanent magnets.
Circuit breakers commonly use electromagnets to operate their mechanisms, not permanent magnets.
Loudspeakers commonly use a permanent magnet to provide a steady magnetic field.
Electric cranes use powerful electromagnets that can be switched on and off.
Magnetic recording typically uses electromagnets in the recording head.

mcqs.stem: A common method used to magnetise a material is:
options: placing inside a solenoid having A.C
rationales: Stroking a material with a magnet in a consistent direction is a common way to magnetise it.
Hitting a material does not reliably magnetise it and can demagnetise it.
Heating generally weakens or destroys magnetisation rather than producing it.
An alternating-current solenoid repeatedly reverses the field and is commonly used to demagnetise a material.

mcqs.stem: A magnetic compass is placed around a bar magnet at four points as shown in figure below. Which diagram would indicate the correct directions of the field?
options: Diagram (a): horizontal bar magnet with N on the left and S on the right; arrows point right above, left at the left, right at the right and left below.
Diagram (b): horizontal bar magnet with N on the left and S on the right; arrows point left above, left at the left, left at the right and right below.
Diagram (c): horizontal bar magnet with N on the left and S on the right; arrows point right above, left at the left, left at the right and right below.
Diagram (d): horizontal bar magnet with N on the left and S on the right; arrows point left above, left at the left, right at the right and left below.
rationales: In diagram (a), the field direction to the right of the south pole and below the magnet is incorrect.
In diagram (b), the arrows above the magnet and to its left do not follow the field from north to south outside the magnet.
In diagram (c), the arrows correctly show the external field emerging from the north pole and entering the south pole.
In diagram (d), the arrows above and to the right of the magnet point in incorrect directions.

mcqs.stem: A steel rod is magnetised by double touch stroking method. Which one would be the correct polarity of the AB magnet?
options: Horizontal bar with N at the left end and S at the right end.
Horizontal bar with S at the left end and N at the right end.
Horizontal bar with N at the left end, S in the middle and N at the right end.
Horizontal bar with S at the left end, N in the middle and S at the right end.
rationales: With the north pole stroking outward toward A and the south pole stroking outward toward B, the resulting poles are N at A and S at B.
This reversed polarity would result if the stroking magnets were oriented the other way around.
A single steel rod magnetised by this method has opposite poles at its ends, not two north poles with a south pole in the middle.
A single steel rod magnetised by this method has opposite poles at its ends, not two south poles with a north pole in the middle.

mcqs.stem: The best material to protect a device from external magnetic field is:
rationales: Wood does not provide effective magnetic shielding.
Plastic does not provide effective magnetic shielding.
Steel can be magnetised and is less suitable than soft iron for shielding a device from an external field.
Soft iron has high magnetic permeability and helps divert external magnetic field lines around the device.
